page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance designed for compute-intensive tasks requiring dedicated processor execution. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz, offering 16 physical cores configured with simultaneous multithreading to deliver 32 dedicated vCPUs. The processor cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache pool. Hardware-level support includes advanced vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server is bundled with 64.0 GB of system memory, 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, one complimentary public IPv4 address, and no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong parallel processing power. Multi-core execution ranks in the upper quartile across both stress-ng (100,519.25) and Geekbench (16,041.0), with single-core stress-ng performance reaching the top 10% tier. In applied workloads, the instance excels in Clang-based software compilation and ray tracing, both placing in the top 25%. Supported vector capabilities also allow for top-tier text generation throughput on small language models (339.19 tokens per second). Conversely, uncached memory bandwidth (124.41 GB/sec read, 67.54 GB/sec write) and transactional database operations in Redis and PassMark fall within median platform averages.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance avoids the resource overhead of memory-heavy instances, improving qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-bound pipelines. A notable engineering tradeoff is that memory capacity is constrained for large in-memory databases or caching layers. However, the inclusion of 500 GB of fast local NVMe storage provides low-latency local disk scratch space. The instance is suited for parallel software compilation, continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, batch processing, media encoding, and distributed compute workloads.
description: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is a compute-focused instance from the Optimized Cloud Compute lineup, powered by a 16-core, 32-thread AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz with dedicated core allocation. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server includes AVX-512 vector instruction extensions and dedicated cryptographic hardware acceleration. It delivers 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, along with 500 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and zero GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance achieves top-quartile results in multi-core compute, software compilation, and ray tracing, while single-core compute reaches top-tier throughput. Memory throughput and static web serving register in the median tier. With dedicated core capacity and fast local NVMe storage, this instance is suited for compute-intensive workloads including continuous integration pipelines, software compilation clusters, parallel batch processing, cryptographic operations, and distributed backend services requiring consistent multi-threaded compute density.
